name: Paris
notes:
LitArbi 0.9.28-beta “Paris” (build 26) — in line with macOS 0.9.28; matters, bundles, Word documents and licences stay interchangeable.
• Insert Citation opens a citation pane docked beside Word (Ctrl+Shift+C). Case names are italic, exhibit numbers bold; full or short form is decided per Word document; awards have their own short form; every document asks for a pinpoint and a pinpoint is never dropped; the exhibit number can go before or after the description.
• Footnotes: space + tab after the number, closing period, hanging indent.
• Update Exhibits from Brief recognises citations copied between footnotes, checks for moved, deleted, merged, missing and duplicate exhibits, and highlights problems in Word with a [LitArbi: …] note. Exhibits are numbered in the order of their first citation.
• List of Exhibits as Word tables, in sections by exhibit type, by appearance or by date.
• Bundles: every non-PDF exhibit (Office, text, e-mail, images) converted to PDF, audio and video copied as-is; index cover, category folders, Mac-style stamp with logo and “Anonymised”, optional signing; an optional submission PDF with clickable links to the cited page or paragraph.
• e-Brief with a clickable index and bookmarks. Redact blacks out every occurrence of a text and flattens the pages. OCR makes scans selectable and searchable in any PDF viewer.
• Menus and a four-tab ribbon regrouped like the Mac; the ribbon adapts to narrow windows. Inspector Files, Notes, Related, References and People tabs; People & Connections graph; column chooser; split a PDF into exhibits; detach attachments; dates that are not dates shown in red.
• Exports (index, chronology, people) identical to the Mac.
